design:
D1 Disturbed is decided per check run, from what that run and its rerun showed. No machine metrics are read: the rule must work in any project and on any machine.
D2 The threshold belongs to each check, beside its report path and rerun command, and defaults to 3. A project with a large suite can raise it, and a check without a report never reaches the rule. On this project's history, 3, 4 and 5 behave the same; 2 would also make the eleven two-test runs disturbed.
D3 A test that is already listed flaky keeps counting as a flake inside a disturbed run, so a real flake that happens to coincide with a busy moment is not lost. Every other test of a disturbed run counts as nothing: no listing, no task.
D4 First flake: the test is listed, so checks do not hold it against anyone's work, and no task is filed. Second flake in a different check run while it is still listed: one fix task is filed. Replayed over this project's 69 flaking runs, threshold 3 with this rule gives 13 tests a task where today's rule gave 79.
D5 No migration. A disturbed run is recorded on the check run's own result and as one event in the Logs. It is deliberately NOT a known-failing entry: an entry with no test excuses every whole-check failure of that check at the gates (`judge_result`, known_failing.py:881-908), and the list allows one such entry per check. A first flake is an ordinary flaky entry with no fix task; "a different run" is read from the entry's `added_by_run`. The threshold is one more field on the check's settings, which are stored as JSON.
D6 Not respecified: one open fix task per test. `_open_fix_task_for` (known_failing.py:328-350) and `fix_tasks_by_test` (flaky_tests.py) already refuse a second open task for a test, including after its entry came off the list; the four-task case above was sequential, not a miss. The requirement drafted for it is retired.

open_questions.question: What makes a run disturbed? Resolved (operator, 2026-11-11): a per-check setting, default 3.
Does a known flake inside a disturbed run still count? Resolved: yes.
When does a single flake get a fix task? Resolved: on its second flake in a separate run.
The existing tasks? Resolved: cleared with the new action once it lands; nothing closed by hand now.

problem:
Code as of agentweave/Architect 9f77d6c (2026-11-11); ledger read from the operator's Hub database read-only the same day.

- **How a check failure becomes a fix task today.** `confirm_failure` (hub/hub/project_checks.py:1177-1250) reruns only the failed tests, alone and once. Each test that passes there goes into `flaky_tests`. `_record_run` (hub/hub/known_failing.py:449-566) then adds a FLAKY known-failing entry for each test and files a high-priority "Fix flaky test <id>" task for each new entry (`_file_fix_task`, :353).
- **Load looks like flakiness.** The rerun runs a handful of tests with no neighbours, so it is nearly unloaded. A test that failed because the whole machine was loaded (git timing out, memory exhausted, a fixed sleep running out) passes there. It is filed as flaky, and nothing distinguishes it from a test that is really nondeterministic.
- **The ledger shows it.** Since 2026-10-26 the Hub has filed 81 fix tasks in this project; 54 are still open (49 pending). Those 54 came from 19 check runs, and six runs produced 38 of them: runs that failed 5, 7, 7, 8, 8 and 10 tests, every one of which passed when rerun. Across all 69 runs that recorded a flake, 52 flaked one test, 11 flaked two, and the other six flaked five or more; none flaked three or four. The three largest affected test files, run alone, passed 102/102 twice.
- **The same test, "fixed" three times.** test_a_turn_start_that_creates_its_checkout_never_stalls_the_loop had four fix tasks filed 11-01 to 11-03. They are not duplicates: each was approved before the next was filed, and de-duplication worked. The test kept failing after three approved fixes, which is what a load-induced failure looks like.
- **A task can quote another test's failure.** Each task's "What the run printed" is the check's (`fix_task_text`, known_failing.py:283-325, reading `failure_excerpt`/`output_tail`), which concatenates every failing test's message. AW-77 names test_a_dependent_lands_after_its_prerequisite but quotes test_a_partial_land_without_a_restart. The report already holds a message for each test (`TestReport.messages`, project_checks.py:701).
- **Stable tests keep their tasks.** A flaky entry comes off the list after 20 consecutive passing runs (`FLAKY_PASSES_TO_CLEAR`, known_failing.py:72), but its fix task stays open by design ("closing it is the operator's"). 19 of the 54 open tasks name a test no longer on the list.

**Why it matters:** a real regression and a busy-machine blip produce the same task. The pile is too large to read, so a real one hides in it, and agents spend turns "fixing" tests that were never broken. Any project with a parallel suite on a shared machine gets this.

requirements.rationale: A failure that hits many unrelated tests at once and vanishes when they run alone is the machine, not the tests: six such runs produced 38 of the 54 open fix tasks.
requirements.statement: When a check run fails at least the check's disturbed threshold of named tests and every one of them passes on the rerun, the Hub records the run as disturbed: the check passes as a flake does today, and no test from it is listed or given a fix task except under FR-8.

requirements.rationale: Not a list entry: an entry with no test would excuse every whole-check failure of that check at the gates (D5).
requirements.statement: A disturbed run is shown on the task's check run, written once to the project's Logs, and shown beside (not in) the Overview's known-failing list for seven days, each naming the check, the run, how many tests failed and passed on the rerun, and the first run's output; it is information, not work: it creates no task and the gates never count it.

A fix task's "What the run printed" quotes the report's failure message for the test the task names, from the run that flaked it; only where the report holds none for that test does it fall back to the check's output, and it then says so.

The operator can close, in one action from the known-failing list, every open Hub-filed flaky fix task whose test is no longer on the known-failing list, each closed with a note naming why; tasks whose test is still listed are left open, and the action says how many it closed and how many it left.
Each check that names a report and a rerun command has a disturbed threshold, a whole number of at least 2, defaulting to 3, shown and changed where the check's report path and rerun command are.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-11: a real flake that coincides with a busy moment must not be lost.
requirements.statement: A test that fails inside a disturbed run and is already on the known-failing list as flaky is treated as flaking again exactly as if the run had not been disturbed.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-11: one flake is a sighting, two are a problem worth a task. Being listed already stops the checks holding it against anyone, so nothing waits on the task.
requirements.statement: A test's first flake in a run that is not disturbed lists it as flaky with no fix task; its next flake in a different check run, while it is still listed, files its one fix task.

in_scope: Recognising a disturbed run: at least the check's threshold of named tests failed in one run and all passed on the rerun
The threshold as a per-check setting, default 3, edited where the check is edited
Recording a disturbed run once, visibly on the check run and in the Logs and Overview, without per-test flaky entries or fix tasks
Keeping an already-listed flake counted when it fails inside a disturbed run
Filing a flaky fix task only on a test's second flake in a separate run
Each fix task quoting its own test's failure message
Closing, in one action, open flaky fix tasks whose test has come off the list, then using it on this project's existing pile
non_goals: Limiting how many checks or agent turns run at once on the machine (the load itself)
Reading machine metrics (CPU, memory) to decide anything
Fixing this repository's own nondeterministic tests (sleep-based waits, Windows lock races): a separate task
Changing how a reproduced failure or a fails-on-main failure is judged
Checks without a JUnit report and rerun command: they rerun whole and never list per-test flakes
Quarantining, skipping or retrying tests automatically
Closing fix tasks whose test is still on the list
Retroactively reclassifying entries already listed from past disturbed runs: they come off as their tests pass 20 runs, and the clear action then closes their tasks
Treating a test id spelled two ways (a dotted and a path form) as one test: seen once in this project, when its report format changed on 2026-11-06

summary: When a check fails many tests at once and every one of them passes when rerun, the Hub records one disturbed run. It does not list each test as flaky or file a fix task for each. A test that flakes is listed at once but gets a fix task only after it flakes in a second, separate run. Each fix task quotes its own test's failure. The operator can close, in one action, every fix task whose test has already proven stable. This applies to any project whose check names a JUnit report and a rerun command.
